author: NEWS10 ABC
title: Man arrested for threatening Fulton Co. Sheriff's Office - NewsBreak
text:
2 hours ago
JOHNSTOWN, N.Y. ( NEWS10 ) — A Northville man was charged following an investigation into a terroristic threat at the Fulton County Sheriff’s Office Communications Center in Johnstown. 40-year-old Patrick Tully was arrested on June 30.
Download our WTEN+ streaming app on Roku, Fire TV and Apple TV! On the same date, at about 9:19 a.m. a Fulton County Sheriff Civil Deputy attempted to serve Tully a paper service at his residence in Northampton. The civil deputy was unable to make contact with him and left the area.
At about 9:44 a.m., the Fulton County Sheriff’s Office Communication Center received a call from an individual who refused to identify themselves. The caller stated that they almost shot the civil deputy and would shoot any other deputies that came to their residence.
Get the latest news, weather, sports and entertainment delivered right to your inbox! Throughout the course of the investigation, it was determined that Tully was the individual who made the call to the communications center. Due to Tully’s comments, as arrest warrant was issued against him for making a terroristic threat.
A temporary extreme risk protection order was granted against Tully, and the New York State Police Special Operations Response Team (SORT) was requested to help take Tully into custody. He was taken into custody at about 4:40 p.m. and turned over to Fulton County Sheriff’s Office Deputies and sent to the sheriff’s office for processing.
He was arraigned in CAP Court and remanded on $5,000 cash bail.
